Import data. 
Format categorical variables to be read by the table calculations.

```{r}
metadata <- read_excel("/metadata/r_all_metadata_output.xlsx")


## Format categorical variables

# Treatment status
metadata <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    treatment_status = case_when(
      treatment_status_final %in% c("complete") ~ "Complete",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("incomplete") ~ "Partial treatment",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("none") ~ "Did not commence",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("unknown") ~ "Unknown",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("unknown if completed") ~ "Partial treatment",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("deceased") ~ "Could not complete",
      treatment_status_final %in% c("none required", "did not want treatment") ~ NA
      )
  )


## Check values for:

# Referral type
metadata %>%
  dplyr::distinct(referral_type) 

# Treatment status
metadata %>%
  dplyr::distinct(treatment_status) 


# Indigenous dentist referral
metadata %>%
  dplyr::distinct(indigenous_dentist)


## Count number of people referred for treatment
metadata %>%
  filter(referral_type %in% c("private", "public")) %>%
  summarise(
    referred_for_treatment = n(),
    treatment_status_recorded = sum(!is.na(treatment_status)),
    treatment_status_missing = sum(is.na(treatment_status))
  )


metadata %>%
  filter(referral_type %in% c("private", "public")) %>%
  count(treatment_status, .drop = FALSE)
```


Format Table 3.
```{r}

## Define the follow-up groups
table_data <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    followup_status = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "yes" ~ "Followed up",
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "no"  ~ "Lost to follow-up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


## Make function to create one section of the table
make_section <- function(data, variable, section_label,
                         eligible = rep(TRUE, nrow(data))) {

  # Baseline counts for eligible participants with recorded data
  baseline <- data %>%
    filter(eligible, !is.na(.data[[variable]])) %>%
    count(category = as.character(.data[[variable]]),
          name = "Baseline")

  # Counts by follow-up status
  followup <- data %>%
    filter(eligible, !is.na(.data[[variable]]),
           !is.na(followup_status)) %>%
    count(
      category = as.character(.data[[variable]]),
      followup_status,
      name = "n"
    ) %>%
    pivot_wider(
      names_from = followup_status,
      values_from = n,
      values_fill = 0
    )

  # Combine baseline and follow-up counts
  result <- baseline %>%
    left_join(followup, by = "category") %>%
    mutate(
      `Followed up` = coalesce(`Followed up`, 0L),
      `Lost to follow-up` = coalesce(`Lost to follow-up`, 0L),
      `Baseline` = paste0(Baseline),
      `Followed up` = paste0(
        `Followed up`, " (",
        sprintf("%.1f", as.numeric(`Followed up`) /
                  as.numeric(Baseline) * 100), "%)"
      ),
      `Lost to follow-up` = paste0(
        `Lost to follow-up`, " (",
        sprintf("%.1f", as.numeric(`Lost to follow-up`) /
                  as.numeric(Baseline) * 100), "%)"
      ),
      section = section_label
    ) %>%
    select(section, category, Baseline,
           `Followed up`, `Lost to follow-up`)

  result
}


## Referral type: all participants with a recorded referral type
referral_table <- make_section(
  table_data,
  "referral_type",
  "Referral type"
)

## Treatment status: only participants referred for treatment
treatment_table <- make_section(
  table_data,
  "treatment_status",
  "Treatment status",
  eligible = table_data$referral_type %in% c("private", "public")
)

## Indigenous dentist referral: only participants referred for treatment
indigenous_table <- make_section(
  table_data,
  "indigenous_dentist",
  "Referral to Indigenous dentist",
  eligible = table_data$referral_type %in% c("private", "public")
)

# Combine sections
table3 <- bind_rows(
  referral_table,
  treatment_table,
  indigenous_table
)


## Print Table 3
table3

```

write.xlsx(

Statistical analysis.
```{r}
## As Fisher's simulated test changes slightly each time, set seed first to ensure reproducibility
set.seed(42)


## Define follow-up variable.
analysis_data <- metadata %>%
  mutate(
    followup_binary = case_when(
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "yes" ~ "Followed up",
      tolower(as.character(followed_up)) == "no"  ~ "Lost to follow-up",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    followup_binary = factor(
      followup_binary,
      levels = c("Followed up", "Lost to follow-up")
    )
  )
 

## Check counts match
table(analysis_data$followup_binary, useNA = "ifany")  # Yes correctly matching.

## Categories to exclude from tests and per-category summaries (compared in lower case)
exclude_levels <- c("did not want treatment") # Those who did not want treatment are dropped due to low number (n = 3)


## Make categorical variables function
drop_excluded <- function(data, variable, exclude = NULL) {
  data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[variable]]),
      !is.na(followup_binary),
      !tolower(as.character(.data[[variable]])) %in% tolower(exclude)
    )
}

test_categorical <- function(data, variable, exclude = NULL, ref = NULL) {

  test_data <- data %>%
    select(all_of(c(variable, "followup_binary"))) %>%
    drop_excluded(variable, exclude) %>%
    droplevels()

  # Reference category first, so OR = "second level vs reference"
  test_data[[variable]] <- factor(test_data[[variable]])
  if (!is.null(ref)) {
    test_data[[variable]] <- relevel(test_data[[variable]], ref = ref)
  }

  tab <- table(test_data[[variable]], test_data$followup_binary)

  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2) {
    return(data.frame(variable = variable, n = sum(tab), test = NA_character_,
                      p_value = NA_real_, cramers_v = NA_real_,
                      v_low = NA_real_, v_high = NA_real_,
                      OR = NA_real_, OR_low = NA_real_, OR_high = NA_real_))
  }

  chi <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))

  if (any(chi$expected < 5)) {
    if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
      result <- fisher.test(tab);                       test_name <- "Fisher's exact"
    } else {
      result <- fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)
      test_name <- "Fisher's exact (simulated)"
    }
  } else {
    result <- chi;                                      test_name <- "Chi-squared"
  }

  es <- as.data.frame(effectsize::cramers_v(tab, ci = 0.95,
                                            alternative = "two.sided"))

  or <- or_low <- or_high <- NA_real_
  if (all(dim(tab) == c(2, 2))) {
    f <- fisher.test(tab)
    or <- unname(f$estimate); or_low <- f$conf.int[1]; or_high <- f$conf.int[2]
  }

  data.frame(
    variable = variable, n = sum(tab), test = test_name,
    p_value = result$p.value,
    cramers_v = es[[1]], v_low = es$CI_low, v_high = es$CI_high,
    OR = or, OR_low = or_low, OR_high = or_high
  )
}

describe_categories <- function(data, variable, exclude = NULL) {
  data %>%
    drop_excluded(variable, exclude) %>%
    group_by(variable = variable, level = as.character(.data[[variable]])) %>%
    summarise(
      n        = n(),
      n_lost   = sum(followup_binary == "Lost to follow-up"),
      pct_lost = 100 * n_lost / n,
      ci_low   = 100 * binom.test(n_lost, n)$conf.int[1],
      ci_high  = 100 * binom.test(n_lost, n)$conf.int[2],
      .groups  = "drop"
    )
}
```



Run analyses.
```{r}
## Check exact labels first, because exclude and ref must match them
unique(analysis_data$referral_type)
unique(analysis_data$indigenous_dentist)


## Referral type: exclude the 3 who did not want treatment (match the label)
res_referral <- test_categorical(analysis_data, "referral_type",
                                 exclude = "did not want treatment",
                                 ref = "private")


## Indigenous dentist referral, among those referred to a private or public clinic
dentist_data <- analysis_data %>%
  filter(referral_type %in% c("private", "public"))

res_dentist <- test_categorical(dentist_data, "indigenous_dentist", ref = "no")


results_table3 <- bind_rows(res_referral, res_dentist)
results_table3   # check n = 402 and n = 327 
```
